Stormwind City, also known as New Stormwind or simply Stormwind, is the capital city of the eponymous kingdom of Stormwind and the largest human city on Azeroth. Located north of Elwynn Forest on Azeroth region's northwest coast, it has become one of the last great human cities after the Third War, and embodies the heart of the Alliance. Stormwind's willingness to work with others to find diplomatic solutions stands out as one of its true strengths. Its citizens hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements and the Alliance against any aggressors.
No city better demonstrates human determination than Stormwind. Destroyed by the Orcish Horde during the First War, the capital was painstakingly reconstructed by the Stonemasons' Guild after the Second War. Parts of the city were eventually razed again when the Dragon Aspect Deathwing provoked the Cataclysm that shattered the world. From the magnificent Cathedral of Light, which serves as a major spiritual hub, to the awe-inspiring Valley of Heroes, which commemorates the sacrifices of Stormwind's loyal champions, the city truly represents the courageous heart of humanity, and serves as a bastion of the Holy Light.
The Stormwind City Guard are the law enforcement and protectors of Stormwind City, keeping the peace within the city's walls.

Located north of [[Elwynn Forest]] on [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth region]]'s northwest coast, it has become one of the last great human cities after the [[Third War]],''[[World of Warcraft: Game Manual]]'', pg. 168 - 170 and embodies the heart of the [[Alliance]].''[[Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 10 Stormwind's willingness to work with others to find diplomatic solutions stands out as one of its true strengths. Its citizens hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements and the Alliance against any aggressors.[https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/human World of Warcraft web site - Human] No city better demonstrates human determination than Stormwind. Destroyed by the [[Old Horde|Orcish Horde]] during the [[First War]], the capital was painstakingly reconstructed by the [[Stonemasons Guild|Stonemasons' Guild]] after the [[Second War]]. Parts of the city were eventually razed again when the [[Dragon Aspect]] [[Deathwing]] provoked the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] that shattered the world. From the magnificent [[Cathedral of Light]], which serves as a major spiritual hub, to the awe-inspiring [[Valley of Heroes]], which commemorates the sacrifices of Stormwind's loyal champions, the city truly represents the courageous heart of [[human]]ity, and serves as a bastion of the [[Light|Holy Light]].[[Image of Wrathion#Quotes|Image of Wrathion's gossip]] The [[Stormwind City Guard]] are the law enforcement and protectors of Stormwind City, keeping the peace within the city's walls.[[The World of Warcraft Townhall/World Map#Stormwind]] {{OTOC|800|240}} ==History== ===Founding of Stormwind=== {{Main|Stormwind (kingdom)}} [[File:Chronicle2 Medivh.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|The [[Guardian of Tirisfal]] [[Medivh]] repelling the [[Jungle troll|jungle trolls]]' invasion of Stormwind City.]] Circa 1,200 [[BDP]],[https://twitter.com/Loreology/status/506857492404391936 Loreology on Twitter] (2014-09-02) (dead link) Stormwind City was founded by [[Faldir]] and the descendants of the [[Arathi tribe|Arathi]] bloodline, who had migrated south from the [[Arathor|Empire of Arathor]] in [[Lordaeron]]. Traveling past the rocky mountains of [[Khaz Modan]], their journey finally ended after many long seasons, and they settled in the northern region of the continent they would name [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth]]. In a fertile valley, they founded the kingdom of Stormwind, which quickly became a self-sufficient power in its own right.[[The Seven Kingdoms]] The capital soon became a sanctuary for the beleaguered refugees driven from their homes.{{Ref WoWCV1|159}} The constant bickering and infighting that marred the rules of the former kings of Arathor had no place in the [[Court of Stormwind|court of Wrynn]], and all had been peaceful for many generations in the kingdom until the [[Gnoll War]]. In 75 BDP, when the [[gnoll]]s assailed the capital in such numbers that few soldiers could be spared to protect the agricultural lands, [[Barathen Wrynn|King Barathen Wrynn]] led his [[knight]]s in battle against [[Garfang|Packlord Garfang]] and scattered the unified packs, solidifying the rule of the [[House of Wrynn|Wrynn dynasty]] over the entire kingdom.{{Ref WoWCV1|160}} In the following decades, Stormwind expanded its borders, much to the displeasure of the [[Gurubashi tribe|Gurubashi]] [[jungle troll]] tribes. Though initially isolated, the [[Gurubashi War|conflict]] quickly escalated out of control in 18 ADP, when [[Llane Wrynn|Prince Llane Wrynn]] led a small party to strike at the Gurubashi leadership in central [[Stranglethorn]]. While the united troll tribes attacked Stormwind City in retaliation, the humans ultimately emerged victorious, largely due to the intervention of the [[Guardian of Tirisfal]] [[Medivh]] who completely destroyed and routed the invaders at the gates of Stormwind City.{{Ref WoWCV2|107|125}} Before the [[First War]] started, Stormwind was a city of considerable size, greater in spread than [[Dalaran]]. Three full sets of walls ribboned around [[Stormwind Keep]], with lesser barriers separating the different wards. Great towers sprang from the streets, and a surging river cascade had been harnessed by massive waterwheels.''[[The Last Guardian]]'', chapter 7 ===The Great Wars=== {{Main|First War|Second War}} [[File:Chronicle Stormwind refugees.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.9|[[Anduin Lothar|Sir Anduin Lothar]] and the [[Refugee|refugees]] fleeing Stormwind for the safety of [[Lordaeron]].]] When reports of mysterious creatures lurking around the [[Black Morass]] reached Stormwind, rumors spread through the streets that they were either vengeful spirits, [[troll]]s armed with some new breed of power, or a strange race from across the [[Great Sea]]. [[Llane Wrynn I|King Llane Wrynn I]] eventually dispatched [[Anduin Lothar|Sir Anduin Lothar]] and his knights to uncover what these new creatures were, resulting in their first clash with the [[orc]]s in what would become known as the [[First War]].{{Ref WoWCV2|119}} In Year 3 ADP, [[Brightwood]], [[Westfall]], and the [[Redridge Mountains]] had eventually fallen, the [[Old Horde|Orcish Horde]] marched onto Stormwind City. After [[Warchief]] [[Blackhand]] ordered [[Kilrogg Deadeye]] and [[Cho'gall]] to lead their [[Bleeding Hollow clan|Bleeding Hollow]] and [[Twilight's Hammer]] clans in the assault, thousands of Horde soldiers marched through [[Elwynn Forest]] and encircled Stormwind, cutting off all access except for the sea. To weaken the city's defenses, [[siege engine]]s bombarded its walls through until dawn, when the orcs finally charged the battlements while [[warlock]]s engulfed Stormwind's soldiers in [[fel]] fire, resulting in staggering losses. As it seemed the capital would fall that day, Lothar and the [[Knights of Stormwind]] caught the orcs in the rearguard by surprise, having moved around the Horde by sea. When the Bleeding Hollow and Twilight's Hammer tried to push them back, Stormwind's large gates opened and soldiers poured out of the city to flank the orcs in a counterattack. Outflanked on both sides and suffering many casualties, the orcs were forced to flee.{{Ref WoWCV2|132}} In Year 4 ADP, a second siege of Stormwind began with orcs breaching the city's walls and fighting in the streets, where the [[Stormwind Army]] was able to hold them at bay. During the fighting, King Llane was assassinated by the assassin [[Garona Halforcen]]. As word of the king's death spread, morale began to fall, and Stormwind was reduced to ashes.''[[The World of Warcraft Pop-Up Book]]'' Returning from slaying the possessed Medivh in [[Karazhan]], Lothar subsequently took on the mantle of regent lord and guided the [[Refugee#Exodus of Stormwind|refugee nation]] in the name of the young prince, [[Varian Wrynn]]. The city's survivors fled to [[Lordaeron]] aboard thousands of boats.''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', first prologue After its destruction, the ruins of Stormwind City were lorded over by the [[orc]]s of the [[Stormreaver clan]].''[[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness]]'' manual, ''[[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness manual#Stormreaver Clan|Clans of the Horde]]'', Stormreaver Clan After the war ended in 6 ADP, special importance was placed on rebuilding Stormwind, and King Terenas officially supported [[Varian Wrynn|Prince Varian Wrynn]]'s ascension to the throne. The kingdom of Stormwind soon became a powerful symbol of humanity's future, and if it could rise from the ashes, anyone could. Its people returned to the ruins of their capital and began to rebuild the once-great city as a testament to their own survival.[[Miss Danna]]'s dialogue in [[Stormwind Keep]] However, word of Stormwind's reconstruction was met with mixed feelings by the kingdom's refugees, and many refused to return to their broken home as it was a reminder of everything they had lost, and instead preferred to start their lives anew in Lordaeron. As the Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron, [[Turalyon]] oversaw the repatriation of the citizens of Stormwind, and helped Varian secure his place as Stormwind's next king by providing him with experienced ministers and advisors,{{Ref WoWCV2|177}} as most of the nobles of the kingdom had been killed by the orcs.''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 3 During the reconstruction, the Alliance called on artisans and patrons to help fund or aid in the massive project, among those who answered were [[Terenas Menethil II|King Terenas Menethil II]],[[The Alliance Splinters]] [[Archbishop]] [[Alonsus Faol]] of the [[Church of the Holy Light|Church of Light]],''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 5[[Alonsus Faol#Death and remembrance|Alonsus Faol's memorial]] and the [[Stonemasons Guild]] contracted by the [[House of Nobles]],[[Report on the Defias Brotherhood]] who restored Stormwind City to its former majesty with white stone for its exterior. Frustrated at the sluggish pace with which [[Ironforge (kingdom)|Ironforge]]'s aid was being delivered to Stormwind, and eager as well to establish a means of reinforcing the human kingdom with dwarven soldiers should the need arise, [[Magni Bronzebeard|King Magni Bronzebeard]] turned to Azeroth's most esteemed engineer, [[High Tinker]] [[Gelbin Mekkatorque]], who immediately began drafting designs for a grand subterranean railway system that would link the cities of Stormwind and [[Ironforge]]. Named the [[Deeprun Tram]], it has since provided swift and safe transportation for thousands of their citizens, allowing military cooperation between both their heroic deeds and to honor their ultimate sacrifice for the safety of Azeroth.[[Valley of Heroes#Statues|Valley of Heroes' statues]] ===Political unrest=== [[File:Tiffindies.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|[[Tiffin Ellerian Wrynn|Queen Tiffin Ellerian Wrynn]] was accidentally killed during the [[Stonemasons Guild]] riots.]] After the [[Stonemasons Guild]] spent years toiling to rebuild the glorious city, they were left broke, as their fees and salaries were left unpaid and unspoken for by the city's officials. When the time of the rightful payment came, the [[nobles of Stormwind]] couldn't because they ran up a huge debt by expanding the military presence through [[Elwynn Forest|Elwynn]] and into [[Stranglethorn Vale|Stranglethorn]], and the massive debt crippled the kingdom's economy.[[Shaw's Report]] In the shadow, [[Onyxia|Lady Katrana Prestor]] manipulated both sides with the [[:Drakefire Amulet]] - her meddling in the rebuilding of Stormwind left the nobility unsatisfied with the craftsmanship of the guild, while the workers were enraged that the nobility despised them and were threatening to withhold payment.{{Ref WoWCV3|36}}[[A Window to the Past]] When [[Edwin VanCleef|Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef]] spoke out, demanding restitution for their works, the [[House of Nobles]] ordered the guild disbanded, which resulted in riots that led to the accidental murder of [[Tiffin Ellerian Wrynn|Queen Tiffin Ellerian Wrynn]]. When [[Varian Wrynn|King Varian Wrynn]] vowed to punish those responsible and dealt with the rioters more severely,{{Ref WoWCV2|136}} the stonemasons fled the city and hid in the rural areas of [[Westfall]], knowing his anger would never fade. The Stonemasons eventually became the terrorist organization known as the [[Defias Brotherhood]], while Lady Prestor used politics and sorcery to politically outmaneuver the king in the coming years. After King Varian went missing under suspicious circumstances, [[Anduin Wrynn|Prince Anduin Wrynn]] was given the crown so that order could be preserved within the realm, at the behest of the royal councilor, Lady Prestor. [[Bolvar Fordragon|Highlord Bolvar Fordragon]] acted as the Regent of Stormwind and the commander of their military forces, with Lady Prestor advising him on the proper use of Stormwind's resources.[[The True Masters (4)]][[Warn Bolvar!]] ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} [[File:Stormwind City Classic.jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.1|Stormwind City in the original ''World of Warcraft''.]] Since the fall of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]], the kingdom of Stormwind has become the strongest bastion of humanity, as well as the most powerful nation within the [[Alliance]]. With the fall of the [[Seven Kingdoms|northern kingdoms]], Stormwind City was by far the most populated human city in the world. Boasting a large population of predominantly human people, Stormwind served in many ways as the cultural and trade center of the New Alliance, which was further supplemented by the capital's access to the sea and its formidable fleet of ships. Racially diverse, heavily populated, an epicenter of culture and trade, Stormwind is acknowledged by many to be the very heart of the Alliance.[[Joining the Alliance]] After [[Azeroth]] had been victim to massive mystic struggles, which tore magic currents from once stable channels, the [[mage]]s of the [[Wizard's Sanctum]] struggled to determine the effects these changes had caused, and some of them feared the worst. When the flow of magic in Stormwind City and [[Elwynn Forest]] was somehow altered, they sent a mage [[adventurer]] to [[Mirror Lake]], in order to test its water for magical properties before those who drank from it would be adversely affected.[[Mirror Lake (quest)]] In {{g|sod}}, a band of [[Burning Blade clan|Burning Blade cultists]] infiltrated Stormwind in order to steal an [[Echoing Orb]] from the [[Knights of the Silver Hand|Silver Hand's]] deepest vault there, but failed in their endeavor. [[Cult of the Damned|Cultists of the Damned]], however, managed to do it themselves, after getting information about the city's secret doors and passageways from disgruntled [[Stonemasons Guild|Stonemasons]].[[Grand Theft Echoing Orb]][[Plaguelands Rendezvous]] Following the first [[Scourge Invasion]], [[Bolvar Fordragon|Regent Lord Bolvar Fordragon]] led an Alliance counterattack, recruiting [[adventurer]]s to raid [[Naxxramas]] and defeat [[Kel'Thuzad]].{{Ref WoWCV3|131}} Prior to the start of the [[invasion of Outland]] in 26 ADP, the gates of Stormwind were invaded by a group of [[Burning Legion]] [[demon]]s led by [[Highlord Kruul]].[[Dark Portal Opens]] ===The Comic=== {{comic-section}} [[File:The Comic - Valley of Heroes.jpg|thumb|upright=.9|Stormwind celebrate the return of their king.]] When the king finally returned, his subjects turned out for a massive ceremony to welcome him home, however, this [[Varian Wrynn]] that returned was arrogant, frivolous, and his freedom was supposedly bought and paid for by a painful new [[tax]].''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 8 ''[[The Return]]'' Once Lo'Gosh, the real Varian, and his allies marched through the gates of Stormwind, they were halted by [[General Marcus Jonathan]] under the direct jurisdiction of Lady Prestor, who ordered their immediate arrest and execution as traitors. After [[Reginald Windsor]] convinced Marcus of his loyalty to the kingdom, Katrana hastily gathered soldiers, only to have the false-Varian tell her that she was not in charge. Within [[Stormwind Keep]], Lo'Gosh revealed that Katrana was in reality the [[black dragon]] [[Onyxia]], and fought against her [[dragonspawn]] disguised as royal guards.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 12 ''[[The Enemy Revealed]]'' Before she escaped, the great black dragon snatched Prince Anduin and teleported them to her [[Onyxia's Lair|lair]]; daring both Varian to follow suit.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 13 ''[[Flashback]]'' After Varian fused back together and used his newly-fused elven sword [[Shalamayne]] to decapitate Onyxia, he ordered her head to be hung from the ramparts of Stormwind City.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 15 ''[[Conflicting Loyalties]]'' ===Wrath of the Lich King=== {{Wotlk-section}} During the second [[Scourge Invasion]] in 27 ADP, the undead stormed [[Stormwind Harbor]], their advance being covered in mists.''[[World of Warcraft: Stormrage]]'', pg. 126 The Scourge army faced the [[Stormwind Army]] and many [[adventurer]]s led by King Varian and [[Bolvar Fordragon|Highlord Bolvar Fordragon]]. When a [[necropolis]] came over them, Varian ordered his magi to create a magical shield over the city, then to cast both spells of fire and ice to create swirling winds, which drove the flying fortress back to the ocean. Meanwhile, [[Magni Bronzebeard|King Magni Bronzebeard]] sent [[goblin]]s in their [[bomber]]s as reinforcements, who managed to destroy the necropolis and many [[frost wyrm]]s.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 19 ''[[The Winds of War]]'' After the [[Battle for Light's Hope Chapel]], the [[death knight]] [[Thassarian]] was treated as an abomination by the population, who threw projectiles, insulted, and spat on him during his walk to [[Stormwind Keep]]. Despite his distrust, King Varian was convinced by [[Tirion Fordring|Highlord Tirion Fordring]]'s letter and ordered that the death knights of the [[Knights of the Ebon Blade|Ebon Blade]] should be treated with respect as former heroes.[[Where Kings Walk]]''[[Death Knight (manga)]]'' At the end of the [[Battle for the Undercity]], [[Jaina Proudmoore|Lady Jaina Proudmoore]] teleported King Varian and the Stormwind Army back to their city, before the Alliance and Horde annihilated each other.[[The Battle For The Undercity (Alliance)]] After the fall of the [[Lich King]], a great ceremony was held within the [[Cathedral of Light]], in honor of the thousands who died in the [[War against the Lich King|Northrend campaign]].''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'', chapter 6 ===Stormrage=== {{Novel-section}} During the [[War Against the Nightmare]], most citizens of Stormwind City were affected by the [[Emerald Nightmare]], who then began to rebuild after the defeat of [[Xavius]].''[[Stormrage]]'' ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} [[File:Deathwing the Destroyer (Twilight of the Dragons) TCG.jpg|thumb|[[Deathwing]] terrorizing Stormwind City.]] During the [[Elemental Unrest]] in 28 ADP, Stormwind City was attacked by furious [[elemental]]s, which were eventually repelled by the kingdom's forces. A meeting of the [[Alliance]] leaders was aksi held in the [[Stormwind Keep]] to discuss the strange natural effects that have been felt across the world. When [[Worried Citizen (Stormwind)|worried citizens]] beseeched the [[Stormwind City Guard]]'s help to find their missing relatives, [[Captain Anton]] reassured the population that their best agents were looking for them, while he and the [[adventurer]]s were investigating the activities of the [[Twilight's Hammer]].[[Speak with Captain Anton]] On the orders of [[King Varian Wrynn|King Varian Wrynn]], the guards eventually interrupted the flow of traffic into the capital and began searching for cultists hiding among the citizens.[[Show Me Your Papers (Alliance)]] All members of the [[Doomsday Cult]] were eventually arrested and taken to the [[Stormwind Stockade]] for questioning.[[Arrest the Infiltrators (Alliance)]] Following the [[Cataclysm (event)|Shattering]], [[Deathwing]] himself descended on Stormwind and burned parts of the city to the ground, only to vanish as quickly as he had appeared.[[Xaxas (song)]] His goal had not been to destroy the human capital, but rather to break its inhabitants so that they could be remade into his servants. Many of Stormwind's fearful citizens sought counsel from [[Archbishop Benedictus]], unaware that he was secretly a member of the Twilight's Hammer, and he subtly guided them into the cult's embrace.{{Ref WoWCV3|200}} During his short appearance, the [[Dragon Aspect]] had crashed down on the city gates, wrecked parts of the city, and blown away the entire [[Park]] after. Afterward, he took the head of Onyxia''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 148 and flew off, something which puzzled the city guardsn as they were certain he would be able to destroy the entire city if he had wanted to.[[Call of Duty (Alliance)#Notes|Call of Duty]] Unnoticed but to cats and ratcatchers, when the mad dragon descended upon Stormwind all the [[Stormwind Rat|rats]] beat a hasty retreat from the city, only of late have they returned.[[Stormwind Rat]] ===Blood of Our Fathers=== {{novel-section}} Not long after [[Deathwing]] attacked Stormwind City, on the day of [[Remembrance Day]], [[Stormwind Harbor]] was full of hulls in every color, shape, and size, as the celebration always brought a host of pilgrims to honor and celebrate humanity's heroes. However, there were even more boats present than usual, as many civilians sought the protection of Stormwind following the ravages caused across [[Azeroth]]. During the celebration, the [[Twilight's Hammer]] cult tried to assassinate both King Varian and Prince Anduin at the [[Stormwind City Cemetery]], where they were lured to by [[Archbishop Benedictus]] under the pretense of family bonding. While the Wrynns fended off the assassins, the Twilight Father Benedictus tried to sway the Stormwind masses to the Twilight Hammer's cause. Inspired by the recent events, King Varian told his people that though he had his faults, as their king, he had and always will have their best interests in mind. Even after the Black Aspect's attack, Stormwind would always remain vigilant and stand defiantly against their enemies, becoming the greatest generation that has ever lived and the heroes of tomorrow. After his speech, Varian watched with pride as his words stirred the hearts of his people, who cheered for this new direction for their kingdom.''[[Blood of Our Fathers]]'' ===Tides of War=== {{Novel-section}} When [[Theramore Isle]] fell, black flags were raised at Stormwind's buildings in honor of those who died there,''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', chapter 20 while mass construction of Alliance ships began in [[Stormwind Harbor]].''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', chapter 21 ===Mists of Pandaria=== {{mop-section}} During the [[invasion of Pandaria]] in 30 ADP, [[Aysa Cloudsinger]] of the [[Tushui]] [[pandaren]] made their way to Stormwind City, where they pledged their allegiance to King Varian. After they joined the [[Alliance]], the Tushui quickly established a presence in the capital near the [[Eastern Earthshrine]].[[An Old Pit Fighter]] Meanwhile, the [[Royal Stonecutters Union]] eventually repaired most of the [[Valley of Heroes]], putting the statue of [[Danath Trollbane]] back in place, however, the ravaged [[Park]] and its surrounding remained in ruins for the time being. ===Warlords of Draenor=== {{wod-section}} When the [[Ironmarch]] assaulted the [[Blasted Lands]] in 31 ADP, [[Warlord Zaela]] and [[Commander Tharbek]], leaders of the [[Black Iron]], took over [[Upper Blackrock Spire]] under the orders of [[Garrosh Hellscream]]. A doomsday weapon was eventually set up within the volcano, which would have induced an eruption to destroy Stormwind City and most of the surrounding area, until the [[adventurer]]s defeated the orcs before they could proceed.[[Upper Blackrock Spire (quest)]] At some point, the [[Kirin Tor]] built a camp on a plateau behind the city walls, overlooking [[Mage Quarter]], which they called the Overlook.[[Everbloom]] map name After a portal was opened to the [[Everbloom]] in {{Au|Draenor|alternate Draenor}}, the [[mage]]s lose control control of the situation, allowing the [[Primals]] led by [[Yalnu]] invaded the city until they were defeated by the adventurers. ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} [[File:Legion Alliance Epilogue - Lion's Rest.jpg|thumb|[[Anduin Wrynn|King Anduin Wrynn]] giving a speech to the people of Stormwind at [[Lion's Rest]] after the [[Argus Campaign]].]] At the start of the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]] in 32 ADP, Stormwind City became the launching point for the [[Alliance]] forces, who prepared themselves in [[Stormwind Harbor]].[[To Be Prepared (Alliance)]] After King Varian died in the [[Battle for Broken Shore]],[[The Battle for Broken Shore (Alliance)]] [[Lion's Rest]] was built over the site of the former [[Park]], where his tomb was displayed along with a memorial for all the fallen Alliance soldiers.''[[Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 16 His son [[Anduin Wrynn]] was then officially crowned as king of Stormwind.[[The Fallen Lion]] When the cultists of the [[Veiled Hand]] infiltrated Stormwind City, the kingdom rulers locked down the capital, until [[Garona Halforcen]] and the [[Adventurer|Shadow]] of the [[Uncrowned]] slain "The Herald", later revealed as [[Melris Malagan|Captain Melris Malagan]] of the [[Stormwind City Guard]].[[The Unseen Blade (Alliance)]] After the [[Argus Campaign]], King Anduin announced the end of the invasion at Lion's Rest,[[Gifts of the Fallen]] while a new [[Stormwind Embassy|embassy]] opened in the [[Stormwind City Outskirts|capital outskirts]].[http://www.scrollsoflore.com/forums/showpost.php?p=1609185&postcount=446/ Blizzcon 2017: Battle for Azeroth Demo] At some point, King Anduin offered pardons and reparations for the former [[Stonemasons Guild|Stonemasons]] and their families.[[Betrayal of the Brotherhood]] who eventually returned to live in the city they once rebuilt.[[A Hungry Heritage]] ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section}} [[File:Stormwind - The Stormwind nobles support him serving as regent and protector of the realm.}} During [[Death Rising]] in 35 ADP, both the [[Argent Crusade]] and the [[Knights of the Ebon Blade]] sent reinforcements to patrol the city, ready to protect its inhabitants in case of an [[undead]] attack.[[Return of the Crusade (Alliance)]] [[Ebon Blade Acolyte]] later established portals to access [[Oribos]] in the [[Shadowlands]] from the [[Wizard's Sanctum]].[[A Doorway Through the Veil]] Following the [[war against the Jailer]] in 36 ADP, Anduin told [[Genn Greymane|King Genn Greymane]] that he couldn't return to [[Azeroth]] yet, entrusting Turalyon to keep Stormwind and the Alliance safe in his absence.[[Penance and Renewal]] ===Dragonflight=== {{df-section}} [[File:Human Heritage Finale Ceremony.jpg|thumb|The [[Lion's Guard]] ceremony in the [[Valley of Heroes]].]] With the return of the [[Dragon Isles]] in 40 ADP, [[Wrathion]] traveled to Stormwind City with the [[Obsidian Warders]] [[dracthyr]], where he met [[Turalyon]] and extended the [[Dragon Aspects]]' invitation to the isles.[[Aspectral Invitation (Alliance)]] Under the lead of [[Toddy Whiskers]], the [[Dragonscale Expedition]] soon gathered various explorers, artisans, and scholars at the [[Stormwind Harbor]],[[Expeditionary Coordination]] and then embarked aboard the ''[[Rugged Dragonscale]]'' for their journey to the ancestral homeland of the [[dragon]]s.[[To the Dragon Isles!]] At some point, [[Count Clessington]] arranged for the [[Defias Brotherhood]] to steal the [[:Drakefire Amulet]] from [[Stormwind Keep]],[[An Urgent Matter]] then used the artifact's powers to turn the bandits against [[Vanessa VanCleef]]. The disgraced noble sought to use [[Northshire Abbey]] as a staging ground to pillage the capital,[[Misdeeds in Moonbrook]] until he was defeated by [[Spymaster]] [[Mathias Shaw]], Vanessa, and the [[adventurer|champion of Stormwind]].[[To Northshire]] As a reward for their heroism, [[General Hammond Clay]] promoted the [[human]] [[adventurer]] into a [[Stormwind Royal Guard|Lionguard]], then bestowed them with a new armor during a ceremony in the [[Valley of Heroes]].[[Go with Honor, Friend]] ===The War Within=== {{Tww-section}} During the [[war in Khaz Algar]] in 42 ADP, [[Turalyon|Regent lord Turalyon]] appointed [[Genn Greymane]] to rule in his stead, leaving him to keep a tight rein on things in his absence.''[[Heartlands]]'', Chapter 5: The Battle of Go'Shek Farm After [[Xal'atath]]'s plan was foiled, [[Anduin Wrynn]] finally returned to Stormwind City but did not reclaim his throne, thereby maintaining the regency under Turalyon.''[[Blood Ties]]'', chapter 2 ===Midnight=== {{Mn-section}} When the [[Twilight's Hammer]] reemerged as the [[Twilight's Blade]], they infiltrated Stormwind and attempted to recruit members out of [[Old Town]], until they were stopped by [[Magister Umbric]].[[Avoiding Blame (Alliance)]] ==Culture== {{Main|Stormwind (kingdom)#People and culture}} ==Inhabitants== {{Main|Stormwind City NPCs}} ==Districts== [[File:VZ-Stormwind City.jpg|thumb|300px|Map of Stormwind City.]] The city is made up of roughly rectangular districts separated by canals. ===Valley of Heroes=== *'''[[The Valley of Heroes]]''' (area beyond and including the city gate) Stormwind is the largest of the surviving human kingdoms remaining on [[Azeroth]]. Connected through both sea access and the newly-built underground railroad, Stormwind proudly swings its doors wide open for adventurers of the entire [[Alliance]]. Among the [[human]]s, many [[Dwarf|dwarves]], [[gnome]]s, [[High elf|high elves]], and [[Night elf|night elves]] and other races live in the capital city, making Stormwind the center of many cultures. Stormwind City's great gates tower over the treetops of Elwynn Forest. Beyond them lies The Valley of Heroes, a beautiful natural basin spanned by a majestic bridge leading to the city's trade district. The bridge is lined with enormous statues depicting some of the greatest heroes of the [[Second War]] — the brave men, high elves, and dwarves who stepped into the [[Dark Portal]] to bring an end to the war in the scarred land of [[Draenor]] itself. As [[Deathwing]] swept over the city during the [[Cataclysm]], he caused great damage to the Valley of Heroes, leaving massive, scorching clawmarks on the nearby towers and toppling the statue of [[Danath Trollbane]] into the water below the bridge. The city's workers eventually finished repairing all of the damages to the valley during the events of the invasion on [[Pandaria]]. ===Trade District=== [[File:The Trade District.jpg|thumb|The Trade District]] *'''[[Trade District|The Trade District]]''' (central district) **'''[[The Gilded Rose]]''' (Stormwind City's inn) **'''[[Northshear Abbey]]''' (Stormwind City's barbershop) "It bustles with trade from across the continent and beyond." The Trade District lies in the center of Stormwind City and is always bustling with activity. It is the place in the city where people can get most goods. Half of the city's banks, auction houses, and inns, as well as the local [[gryphon]] master, are all located within. In addition, consumers find plenty of outlets for their coin in the various equipment shops nearby. For those with a taste for the delectable, the [[Trias]] and Gallina families run cheese and wine shops out of the Trade District as well. ===Old Town=== [[File:Old Town.jpg|thumb|The Old Town]] *'''[[Old Town]]''' (eastern district) **'''[[Champions' Hall]]''' (Alliance PvP barracks) **'''[[Training Hall]]''' (trainers) ***Originally: '''[[Command Center]]''' (warrior and hunter guilds) **'''[[SI:7]]''' (rogue guild) To the east of the Trade District is the Old Town, the oldest section of the capital, and many parts of it still predate the reconstruction of the city after its razing by the orcs during the events of the [[First War]]. As the district had not been badly ravaged, it had never needed true rebuilding. Consequently, it is a rustic, downtrodden place, where the streets are described as far dirtier and smellier than the other districts. It is also the residential area for most of the poor folk of the city, as beggars, thieves, and the poor can be found there.''[[Stormrage]]'', chapter 21 Fortunately, the Stormwind [[Command Center]] is located along the edges of the quarter, and near is the headquarters of the [[SI:7]], the kingdom's intelligence agency. ===Mage Quarter=== [[File:The Mage Quarter.jpg|thumb|The Mage Quarter]] [[File:Stormwind's new Portal Room.jpg|thumb|The new [[portal]] room in [[patch 8.1.5]].]] *'''[[Mage Quarter]]''' (western district) **'''[[The Slaughtered Lamb]]''' (warlock guild) **'''[[Wizard's Sanctum]]''' (mage guild) **'''[[Academy of Arcane Arts and Sciences]]''' (mage guild) To the west of the Trade District is the Mage Quarter. The [[Wizard's Sanctum]] stands proudly in the center of the district, it is here that [[mage]]s train to increase their powers, while shady [[warlock]]s are often drawn to the dark cellars of the [[Slaughtered Lamb]], where they practice their [[Shadow (magic)|dark]] [[Fel|arts]] in the shadows of polite society.[[Visiting Warlock#Quotes|Visiting Warlock's gossip]] The rest of the district is filled with tailoring shops, warehouses storing magical artifacts and reagents, and bustling coffeehouses and bars. During the [[First War]], Stormwind utilized the services of the mysterious [[conjurer]]s, but they no longer have any presence in the city. ===Cathedral Square=== [[File:Cathedral Square.jpg|thumb|The Cathedral Square]] *'''[[Cathedral Square]]''' (northern district) **'''[[Cathedral of Light]]''' (Paladin/Priest guild) **'''[[Stormwind City Cemetery]]''' **'''[[Orphanage (Stormwind City)|Orphanage]] To the north of the Trade District is Cathedral Square, the religious center for all followers of the [[Light|Holy Light]]. Though Stormwind Keep is the biggest structure in Stormwind City, many believe the most awe-inspiring is the Cathedral of Light. Within the cathedral are the most faithful and true [[paladins]] and [[priests]] of the human race. The bishops and paladins at the cathedral are on a lifelong quest to bring the light to the darkest places on [[Azeroth]], and all are welcome within the cathedral's walls as long as their journey is one of good and not evil. Other notable locations in the square include the city's orphanage, and the [[City Hall]], where Stormwind's architects and researchers keep a census on the citizens of the kingdom, as well as finding ways to improve the quality of life for those within the city. ===Dwarven District=== [[File:The Dwarven District.jpg|thumb|The Dwarven District]] *'''[[Dwarven District]]''' (north-eastern district) **'''[[Deeprun Tram]]''' (accessible from the Dwarven District) To the east of Cathedral Square is the Dwarven District, where the dwarves and gnomes of [[Ironforge]] carve a slice of Stormwind life out for themselves. The air is thick with smoke and sparks, and the ground trembles with the pounding of anvils, but to many it feels just like a home should. A trove of weapon and armor shops line the streets, and [[Smith|blacksmiths]] create masterpieces out of common metals in the many open-air plazas. Many adventurers pass through the Dwarven District on their way to the Deeprun Tram, a marvel of [[gnomish]] [[engineering]] and fast transport to the city of Ironforge. The massive spinning cog that frames the entrance to the tram tunnel cannot be missed. An opening by the northern end leads to the [[Stormwind City Outskirts]], a small rural area outside the walls of the city. ===Canals and the prisons=== *'''[[Canals (Stormwind City)|The Canals]]''' (separating all districts) **'''[[Vault (Stormwind City)|The Vault]]''' **'''[[Stormwind Stockade]]''' ('''[[instance]]''' accessible from the Canals, north-east of the Mage Quarter) **'''[[Cut-Throat Alley]]''' (accessible from The Canals; empty) Each district is bordered by shimmering blue canals and linked by bridges spanning over them. Anglers fish from the many docks in the city, the freshwater fish within perfect quarry for the beginning fisherman. There are two fortifications that rise from the waters in Stormwind - both are prisons for the lawless and evil. [[The Stockade]] is accessible from the Mage Quarter and holds murderers, gnolls, thieves, and other enemies of the kingdom. A similar prison, the [[Vault (Stormwind City)|Vault]], is surrounded by water on all sides and seems to be holding out fine - for now. ===Stormwind Keep=== [[File:Stormwind Keep Post Cata.jpg|thumb|Stormwind Keep]] *'''[[Stormwind Keep]]''' (between Old Town and the Dwarven District) **'''[[Petitioner's Chamber]]''' **'''[[Royal Library]]''' (library) **'''[[War Room]]''' (Alliance PvP battlemasters) Finally, the crown of Stormwind City remains Stormwind Keep. Rising high between the Dwarven District and Old Town, the keep is the seat of power of the kingdom and serves as the residence of the Stormwindian kings, currently King [[Anduin Wrynn]]. The [[Court of Azeroth|royal court]] as well as some of the [[House of Nobles|nobles]] of the kingdom are also here. The Keep offers a view of the whole city, so that the king can watch over the masses, and provide a powerful reminder of what deserves to be defended.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 12 Within the keep itself are many librarians, nobles, and representatives of the human peoples as well as the [[battlemaster]]s. ===Stormwind Harbor=== [[File:Sharbour.jpg|thumb|Stormwind Harbor]] *'''[[Stormwind Harbor]]''' (north-west of the Cathedral Square) The harbor is located in the most northern area bordering the [[Great Sea]], with the access point set between the Park and Cathedral Square. Stormwind City towers over the harbor, with cannons stationed all along the walls. A major transportation hub, the docks are teeming with all sorts of activity. [[Siege engine]]s are also dotted throughout the area, and at the northern tip one can find a large [[shipyard]]. If you are friendly enough, [[Thargold Ironwing]] will grant you a free aerial tour through the entire region. ===Stormwind City Outskirts=== [[File:Stormwind Embassy.jpg|thumb|The Stormwind Embassy]] *'''[[Stormwind City Outskirts]]''' (north of the Dwarven District) **'''[[Stormwind Embassy]]''' **'''[[Wollerton Stead]]''' **'''[[The Eastern Earthshrine]]''' This area has been built as a replacement for the [[Stormwind Park]], swallowed by [[Deathwing]]'s assault on the city. It houses a large lake with several farmhouses, as well as an [[Earthen Ring]]'s earthshrine, which served for [[adventurer]]s to teleport on the fronts of the [[war against Deathwing]]. The [[Tushui Pandaren]] have set up a pavilion near the earthshrine, where adventurers can travel to [[Pandaria]], purchase [[dragon turtle]] mounts and contains the city's [[monk]] class trainer. It shares the same beauty as the rest of [[Elwynn Forest]]. Following the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]], a new embassy for the [[Allied race|new allies]] was built in the outskirts. After the [[Burning of Teldrassil]], the displaced night elves and humans of Gilneas largely took refuge in this area, with their racial vendors being located here. ===Lion's Rest=== [[File:Lion's Rest.jpg|thumb|The Lion's Rest]] *'''[[Lion's Rest]]''' (southwest from Cathedral Square or northwest from the Mage Quarter.) From the quest [[Cataclysm in the Catacombs]], the Cathedral of Light is phased, with Warped and Babbling Cultists and the target of the quest, [[The Black Bishop]], in place of the many NPCs and trainers. ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} [[File:AzerothLoC.JPG|thumb|The region of Azeroth in ''[[Lands of Conflict]]''.]] ===Name=== The city is named for the occasional sudden squalls created by a ley line pattern in the mountains around the city.[[More Magic and Mayhem]], pg. 47 ===Stormwind region=== '''Stormwind''' is the name of a region''[[Horde Player's Guide]]'', pg. 9 (land''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 125, 214 or area.''[[Monster Guide]]'', pg. 20) It is a small, coastal zone west of the [[Burning Steppes]], south of [[Dun Morogh]] and northwest of [[Elwynn Forest]], on the western coast[[World of Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]], pg. 13 of the [[Eastern Kingdoms]]. This region is the location of Stormwind City, as established in ''[[Lands of Conflict]]''''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 52 and ''[[Warcraft The Roleplaying Game]]'',[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]], pg. 215 and includes an area north of the city.[[:File:AzerothLoC.JPG]] Today, with the collapse of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] and [[Stromgarde (kingdom)|Stromgarde]], Stormwind is the brightest bastion of humanity on [[Azeroth]]. The mountains around the glorious Stormwind Keep have an impressive ley line pattern that is responsible for the occasional sudden squalls that give Stormwind City its name. Wild beasts including harpies and dire wolves inhabit this area.[[More Magic and Mayhem]], pg. 47 The Stormwind region itself does not go much beyond the boundaries of Stormwind City; it begins at the [[Valley of Heroes]] and extends into the mountains to the north.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 52, 53 The city stands firm on [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth]]'s northwest coast and is the capital of both the Stormwind region and [[Stormwind (kingdom)|kingdom]], and contain one of the few remaining great human cities. Primarily a human settlement, a fair number of [[High elf|high elves]], [[Ironforge dwarf|Ironforge dwarves]], and even a few [[Night elf|night elves]] and [[gnome]]s dwell here as well. A reasonably [[Stormwind Harbor|large shipyard]] lies on the northwestern part of the city and provides the Alliance with naval craft. The lush valley of heroes lies south of the city and all visitors must pass through it, as it is the only entrance to Stormwind on foot. With all the rebuilding efforts in the past thirty years, the city has several notable structures. These include: the [[Academy of Arcane Sciences]], [[Cathedral of Light]], [[Pig and Whistle]], the [[Stockade]] and the [[Vault (Stormwind City)|Vault]], and [[Stormwind Keep]]. The mighty walls surrounding Stormwind are somewhat invulnerable to small scale attacks. Crossbowmen can be stationed upon the ramparts, heavy [[ballista]]e keep watch for enemy artillery, and of course, waves of guards are willing to sacrifice their lives to defend the city.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 53 A grand city with new construction that still gives a nod to human and dwarven architecture of old, one can move about Stormwind on foot, rent one of many mounts or even have a small boat take them through the several canals that bisect the city. The mountains north hold some nastier sorts of beasts that will sometimes venture south to see what they can pick from the road. The passage is no stranger to [[harpy]] attacks, and even dire wolves are spotted north of the city. The locals assume the creatures have escaped from the Blackrock orcs in the Burning Steppes. ===People and culture=== [[File:Unusedwestzone.JPG|thumb|left|The [[Northern Elwynn Mountains|mountains]] north of Stormwind City.]] Stormwind is the jewel of the Alliance in Azeroth. The oldest and grandest human city, it has weathered three wars, ransacking by the orcs, and invasions by the Alliance to take it back. Although mostly a human city, Stormwind does house [[Dwarf|dwarves]], [[high elf|high elves]], [[night elf|night elves]], and other Alliance races. It opens its gates to all Alliance members to participate in trade within the city limits. Most of the city's coffers are filled with the [[tax]]es taken from merchants in the busy market. Every night at sunset the Cathedral of Light rings a solitary bell whose sweet pitch reaches the entire city. This is for the night elves, who are unaccustomed to living within cities. A day of mourning is set aside for the high elves, remembering Dalaran's destruction. The ale pours free for every dwarf in the city during the holy birthday of Anvil Stormglaive. It also holds celebrations for the Third War veterans, to honor the citizens of all Alliance races who fought in the war. Stormwind's climate is warm, the skies clear, and the seasons generally temperate. Thus, clothes in the city are composed of light fabric for the most part. Color choices usually are bold: whites, reds, blues, oranges, and yellows. Although one might assume the climate would call for as little clothing as possible, the inhabitants of Stormwind prefer light fabric, but lots of it. Humans usually wear long-sleeved tunics, billowy trousers, leather boots, and sometimes even ridiculously large, floppy hats for excessively sunny days. The high elves generally copy the humans' fashions here, though there are some high elves who prefer to set themselves apart. Although Stormwind is well-defended, the city guard usually wears only light armor to handle the occasional thief or bandit. The paladins will don their full plate during ceremonies and when they ride out of the city on business defending Elwynn Forest or the surrounding areas, but around the city they wear nothing more than the breastplate that identifies them as paladins. A third force in the city is dedicated to maintaining the peace. In addition, a guild of assassins works behind the scenes with the blessings of the king and the Stormwind ruling council. When solving an "inconvenient" problem would go against the tenets of the Holy Light, the [[Stormwind Assassins]] are called. They deal with matters quickly and efficiently, and few questions are asked. The city's nobility strives for power while manipulating others and shrouding their sins in secrecy. A few exceptional nobles, however, do try to tend to the city the best they can. The priests, meanwhile, uphold the tenets of the Holy Light, although some have become more political than religious. The guard is generally uncorrupted and has a close relationship to the carefree citizens of Stormwind. Opposition to the Horde, Scourge, Burning Legion, and Shadow are near requirements to live in the city. Anyone who speaks out in support of these groups, or even suggests it, is likely to be hanged or driven out, for these beliefs are enforced like law by the will of the common man. Most citizens of the city are practitioners of the Holy Light, and nearly all at least respect it. The religion is tied closely to the government, for the church has enough political influence to directly impact the actions the King decides to take. Those criminals who survive arrest and trial reside in one of the city's two prisons. Common criminals from pickpockets to murderers stay in the Stockade. More dangerous types — demons, rogue mages, and the like — are left to rot in the Vault, which is surrounded on all sides by water.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 52 - 53 ==Notes and trivia== [[File:150px-Perfect flag of Stormwind.jpg|thumb|The Stormwind banner]] ;Lore *[[Doctor Weavil]] refers to Stormwind City as the "capital of cheese",[[Diary of Weavil]] likely because of the shop [[Trias Cheese]]. *The cathedral's bell rings to mark the hours, and in times of danger to alert the citizens.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 17 *[[SI:7]] have "friends" in nearly every quarter of Stormwind City, selling goods, listening to strangers chat, and keeping an eye out on their behalf.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 10 - 11 *Fishing is a favored sport in Stormwind City. The canals and lakes of Stormwind City house a variety of seafood. Fishermen fish [[Gigantic Catfish]][[A Fisherman's Feast]] and [[Canal Crab]]s[[Feeling Crabby?]] in the [[Canals (Stormwind City)|Canals]]. [[Olivia's Pond]] is stocked with [[Crystal Bass]] every year[[Diggin' For Worms]] and Stormwindians have recently been trapping [[Rock Lobster (quest item)|Rock Lobsters]] below the docks of [[Stormwind Harbor]].[[Rock Lobster (quest)]] The most prized and challenging fish is the [[Hardened Walleye]], found in [[Stormwind Lake]].[[Hitting a Walleye]] *The artillery shells used by the ''[[Storm's Fury Wreckage|Storm's Fury]]'' [[gunship]] were manufactured by the "[[Stormwind Royal Industries]]".[[Gunship Down]] *The [[Slaughtered Lamb]]'s basement and catacombs serve as host to the [[Slaughtered Lamb coven|warlock community]] of Stormwind.[[You Have Served Us Well]] *In some districts, School Mistress [[Miss Danna]] teaches a group of [[children]], indicating the presence of a [[school]] in the city. *Apple trees can be found in every district of Stormwind City.[[The King's Cider]] *A sewer in the city leads to [[Mirror Lake]].[[On Track]] *The [[Four Dons]] used to sing in the city.[[Rohan the Assassin]] when asked about the [[Bonescythe Armor]] ;Gameplay *Stormwind City is arguably the largest city in the game after the addition of Stormwind Harbor and the Outskirts. Since patch 1.10, it has risen in popularity compared to Ironforge (though this may vary by server). Stormwind City is now only two boat rides (or a tram ride) away from every other Alliance city as well as Northrend, making it extremely attractive to adventurers of all races. It became even more suited in ''Cataclysm'' which removed the city portals in [[Dalaran]] (and [[Shattrath]]) while adding the [[Eastern Earthshrine]] to Stormwind City. The removal of the city portals reduced especially Dalaran's popularity as a hangout spot (Shattrath lost its popularity in WOTLK when it was "replaced" by Dalaran) which made other cities closer to the new areas more attractive. [[Orgrimmar]] has undergone the same process for Horde players. *From [[patch 3.0.8]] to [[patch 4.0.3]], [[Night elf|night elves]] and [[draenei]] could only ride through Stormwind City's [[Stormwind Counting House]] bank door on [[mechanostrider]]s; all other Alliance mounts made these two races too high to fit. When it was remodeled with the addition of the [[Dwarven District]]'s [[Royal Bank of Stormwind]] in [[patch 4.0.3a]], the height of the doorway was increased. *The part of this region that doesn't include Stormwind City was inaccessible in ''[[World of Warcraft]]'' before [[patch 4.0.3a]], in which it was finally removed and replaced with water. **North of this area, on the other side of Coldridge in Dun Morogh, is a long valley that continues northward behind the mountain entrance of Gnomeregan. Kazzak has since been moved to [[Hellfire Peninsula]]. *There was once an endless supply of [[Ice Cold Milk]] scattered around Stormwind City in barrels, which was useful if you were a low-level mana user and wanted to save gold. ;Miscellaneous *See [[Stormwind City NPCs]] for a list of quest givers in the area. *In the map of ''[[Warcraft: Orcs & Humans]]'' this region is represented by [[Stormwind Keep]], some mountains and an unmarked forest. *The [[World of Warcraft World Map]] released by [[BradyGames]] shows the northern part of the region as being mountainous. *Before its destruction, the [[Park]] was the largest area outside of Kalimdor dedicated to and inhabited by [[Night elf|night elves]]. *The gnome warlock [[Niby the Almighty]] was previously planning to unleash a demon upon Stormwind City as punishment for exiling him. Although he managed to summon the [[El Pollo Grande|Black Chicken of Death]], it seems he gave up his plans and later moved to [[Icecrown Citadel]], where he now sells [[Tier 10]] armor for warlocks. *Stormwind City is [[Stormwind City (Drums of War)|a rare location card]] in the [[World of Warcraft: Trading Card Game]]'s [[Drums of War (TCG)|Drums of War]] set. *One of the classic game boards in ''[[Hearthstone (game)|Hearthstone]]'', ''{{Hs|United in Stormwind}}'', is themed around Stormwind City. ;Development *When developing Stormwind during the creation of ''World of Warcraft'', the designers didn't know what gameplay purpose the in-game cities would serve, only that the game would have large capital cities (though no one seemed to know exactly how big the cities needed to be). At the time, the developers thought that all quest givers would be located in the cities, though they later realized that this didn't make any sense from a design standpoint. [[Johnathan Staats]] recalls that Stormwind was "especially painful" to design due to its confusing layout and the fact that the [[minimap]] functionality didn't exist for the majority of WoW's development, meaning that many who entered Stormwind would get lost and be unable to find the city gates. He cites the specific example of not being able to tell that one was in the [[Trade District]] until one saw the gates leading out of the city.{{Ref web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L77uPm5cuTo&t=1h13m22s|title=John Staats Interview - The World of Warcraft Diary (1:13:22)|work=YouTube|author=MMO-Champion|date=2018-09-24|accessdate=2018-09-24}} *Staats also recalls that Stormwind may have originally had nine districts, two of which were fused into a single area. *Originally, the city was planned to feature gondolas that would serve as a quick way to travel from one district to another, hence the existence of the Canals and the fact that players can get in and out of the Canal waters.
